newsitem.title: UK: No soft oil supply problems seen by European trade.
newsitem.headline: No soft oil supply problems seen by European trade.

text.p: Traders on the European vegetable oil market do not foresee any problems for local soft oil output despite concerns in the U.S. over soybean supplies.
Chicago soybean prices hit limit up during early trading on Thursday and finished sharply higher on renewed concerns that U.S. soybean supplies would not last out the summer months.
Traders based their fears on a drop of deliverable soybeans to 35,000 bushels on Thursday against 1,245,000 the previous day.
However, in Europe traders could see no problems with supplies reaching the crushers.
"At this time of year European crushers are operating almost wholly on south American beans and there are no problems there," said one.
Traders said loading time in south American ports was down to three days for soybeans.
Earlier in the year there had been some concern over the European rape crop which looked as if it was going to be affected by drought in the U.K. and France but this situation has now eased.
"We have had some reasonable rainfall and now the weather is getting warming up, making almost prefect growing conditions for rapeseed," said another trader.
Estimates of this year's crop range between 7.50 to 8 million tonnes, traders said.
"It looks like it's going to be a very good crop this year," said one trader.
Traders said there was nothing to stop prices going up on the back of the Chicago market.
"Chicago will have an effect and we are seeing demand for China but nothing unusual." said a trader. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8062
